startup.name: SpaceFlow Technologies, Inc.
startup.one_liner: AI-native procurement services for the physical economy
startup.description: SpaceFlow is a services company that uses AI to run procurement work for manufacturers, logistics and other physical goods businesses: bringing more spend under management, doing source to contract work and turning identified savings into realised savings without adding staff or replacing systems. Customers pay for services, likely a share of savings. Team of 4 in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Accepted to YC in this test, so this note is for completeness. From roughly 1 percent for a random applicant, the lift is a clear painful problem and a savings based offer. The cuts are a team of 4, no stated customers or revenue, and a services model that YC partners usually view as less scalable than software.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because the pitch is a services business with AI on top rather than a product, it names no customers or realised savings, and procurement software is a well served field with Zip and others, which makes a four person team look unlikely to win.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only gave seed cond 59% (n=126), range 49 / 59 / 65%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Under the anchor because a services model with a four person team and no stated revenue is harder to fund, though AI enabled services is a 2026 investor theme.

bands.rationale: Thin or small-check round, close to the standard YC deal plus a small angel or pre-seed extension, typical when traction is slow.
Core case: 2022+ seed medians in the researched cohort are about $3.2M raised, and 2026 public seed pre money medians are near $18M.
Upside: a hot-category seed led by a top seed fund after quick early revenue or usage.
Outlier large seed, seen in the hottest AI categories only and rare overall.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed above $500K does not close if investors treat it as a consultancy with software margins promised, if no customer shows realised savings in the first six months, or if the sales cycle for procurement services is long. SourceBeacon, a procurement concierge, never raised after YC, and Mentum only raised a seed before a quick sale.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only gave series_a cond 26% (n=74).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Under the anchor because services businesses scale with headcount and Series A investors want software margins.

bands.rationale: Modest A or a down-leaning round after a slow year of growth.
Core case: 2022+ YC series A medians are about $15M raised, public series A pre money near $60M.
Upside A led by a large fund after strong, fast revenue growth.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails if gross margin stays like a services firm, if each customer needs bespoke work, or if savings realisation depends on customer behavior that the startup does not control. Zip reached late rounds as software, which shows what Series A investors prefer, and Alpas stayed at seed with a software product.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only gave series_b cond 16% (n=19); full sample cond 44% (n=126).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Between the young B2B cohort and the full sample, since a company that survived to A has paying customers.

bands.rationale: Smaller or flat B, often an extension for a company that is profitable but growing slower.
Core case: 2022+ YC series B medians are about $37M to $45M raised.
Upside B on fast growth in a large category, led by a major growth fund.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B fails if growth is linear with headcount, if large consulting firms and procurement outsourcers compete on price, or if software vendors add agents that do the same work. Savings based fees are lumpy and make revenue hard to forecast for investors who expect steady recurring contracts.

anchors.adjustment_reason: A bit under the full sample conditional because few services led companies reach late rounds.

bands.rationale: Smaller late round or a growth extension, likely when growth has slowed but revenue is solid.
Core case: 2022+ YC series C medians are about $45M raised, public series C deal size near $77M.
Upside late round for a category leader with fast growth and strong retention.

ladder.why_it_fails: A later round fails if the company stays a services shop, if procurement leaders in the target industries buy suites from Zip or Coupa instead, or if the savings pool per customer shrinks. Late rounds usually go to products with high net retention and clear software margins, which a services company rarely shows.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The likeliest result is a stall as a small services firm or a quiet sale to a procurement software or consulting company, because outcome based services scale slowly. A result above $1B would need SpaceFlow to become a software platform that replaces a large part of procurement suites, which is far from a four person services start.

analogs.relevance: AI assistant for procurement and strategic sourcing, Summer 2021.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a seed and was acquired.
Shut down with no round after YC, a services style procurement failure.

analogs.relevance: B2B spend and procurement intake software, Summer 2020.
analogs.outcome_summary: Reached a Series D or later round, the software outcome in the category.

analogs.relevance: Software to find suppliers for procurement departments, Winter 2021.
analogs.outcome_summary: Active with only a seed found, a modest outcome.

killers.risk: Services model never reaches software margins
killers.evidence: Source to contract work and savings capture are labor heavy, and investors price services at far lower multiples than software.
killers.mitigation: Productise repeat workflows and price on software like recurring contracts.

killers.risk: Procurement software suites and AI agents absorb the work
killers.evidence: Zip, Fairmarkit and Keelvar already sell AI sourcing, and Zip and Fairmarkit announced a partnership, per the market search.
killers.mitigation: Focus on physical goods categories the suites handle poorly and show realised savings.

killers.risk: Founders cannot sell long enterprise procurement cycles with four people
killers.evidence: Procurement buyers move slowly and want references, and a four person team has limited capacity for sales and delivery.
killers.mitigation: Start with a few design partners paid on savings and use their results as references.

competition_now.name: Zip and Fairmarkit
competition_now.what: Intake orchestration and autonomous tail spend sourcing software.
competition_now.traction: Established vendors; they announced a partnership in April 2026.

competition_now.name: Keelvar and Globality
competition_now.what: Sourcing event automation and services spend sourcing.
competition_now.traction: Keelvar says 85 percent of its customers' sourcing work is automated, a vendor claim.

competition_now.name: Status quo: in house buyers and consulting firms
competition_now.what: Procurement teams and consultants do sourcing manually or with spreadsheets.
competition_now.traction: The default for most physical goods firms.

technical_complexity.rationale: The AI work (reading contracts, finding suppliers, running sourcing events) is buildable by a small team with current models, and the hard part is trust, integration with existing systems and delivering realised savings, not technology.

takeover_risk.rationale: Suites can add agents quickly, but a services layer that owns delivery is not their model, so copying takes longer for the services piece than for the software.

evidence.claim: Procurement teams are buying AI agents for intake, sourcing and negotiation in 2026, showing budget for the category.
Vendors report that sourcing work can be largely automated, so buyers expect AI savings.

roadmap.goal: Land two paying design partners with measured savings.
actions: Sign pilots paid on realised savings.
Write a case study with the dollar savings.
roadmap.proof: Two customers with documented realised savings.

roadmap.goal: Show repeatable delivery and a seed above $500K.
actions: Turn the common workflows into reusable software.
Report gross margin and hours per dollar saved.
roadmap.proof: A seed above $500K and gross margin above 50 percent on services.

pros.point: Aligned to a clear dollar benefit.
pros.evidence: Savings based pricing ties fees to results, which buyers like.

pros.point: AI enabled services is an active investor theme in 2026 and procurement has budget.
pros.evidence: Many AI procurement tools are marketed and bought in 2026.

brand.name: SpaceFlow Technologies, Inc.
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "SpaceFlow Technologies" --era 2022+ gave kind name_plus_descriptor, 21 chars, 3 words, descriptor word technologies.
strengths: SpaceFlow is a short compound word
weaknesses: Legal name carries Technologies and Inc
brand.rationale: The compound SpaceFlow is acceptable but suggests the wrong industry, and the legal suffixes make it generic; a weak name rarely sinks a B2B services company, so the effect is neutral.

narrative.headline: A four person AI procurement services company with a thin pitch, so seed is a toss up and software margins are unproven.
narrative.general_summary: SpaceFlow offers AI assisted procurement services to manufacturers and logistics firms, taking on sourcing and contract work and converting savings into realised savings. The pain is real and the category has budget, but the batch start picture is thin: four people, no named customers and a services model that investors price at lower multiples. Zip shows that software can win in the category, and SourceBeacon shows that a concierge model can fail. A seed is possible if early customers show realised savings, and the later steps depend on moving from services to repeatable software. A stall as a small services firm is the most likely path, and a sale to a procurement vendor is the main alternative.

assumptions: Forecast made blind from the batch start 2026-07-06 using only the input file and market searches.
Seed means a round above about $500K within about 12 months.
The services model and savings based pricing are inferred from the description.
Cohort anchors for 2022 to 2025 B2B are young and later stages are weak.
